title: Ansel and the Smile
premise: Noor Halloran returns to the frost-bound town of Vesper Hollow to bury their twin Ansel, only to find the body in the casket wearing Noor's face — and Ansel alive at the family house, insisting he never died. The Hallorans were founding families of a ritual that holds back something beneath the frost, and every mirror on the property has begun lagging one second behind reality, showing rooms where things move before they move. As Noor and Ansel unravel which twin actually survived, they discover the ritual demands a willing sacrifice from their bloodline, and their late mother's found family of town elders intends to collect it. In the end, Noor and Ansel refuse to choose between love and duty: together they complete the ritual as two offerings instead of one, sealing the frost with a bond it cannot split, though one mirror is left permanently empty.
about_author: Xanthe Lockridge is the pen name of a former mortuary assistant from rural Vermont who writes horror about houses that remember too much. Their short fiction has appeared in small-press anthologies, and 'Ansel and the Smile' is their first novel.

chapters.title: The Wrong Face in the Casket
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor arrives in Vesper Hollow for the funeral and lifts the casket lid to find their own face staring back. The town's condolences feel rehearsed, and Aunt Maren watches Noor too closely. Emotional beat: grief curdling into dread as the first crack appears in what Noor believes is true.

chapters.title: Ansel at the Window
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. At the family house, Noor sees Ansel standing at an upstairs window — alive, smiling exactly the way he smiled as a child. He claims he never died and begs Noor not to tell the elders he's home. Emotional beat: joy shadowed by terror; the smile feels both beloved and wrong.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The mirrors begin lagging: reflections trail reality by a heartbeat, and in them, figures stand in rooms seconds before anyone enters. Ansel insists the house always did this, that Noor simply forgot. Emotional beat: gaslit unease; loyalty to Ansel strains against the evidence of Noor's eyes.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel searches the attic and finds the founders' ledger: seven families, a ritual written in frost-patterns, and a page torn out bearing the Halloran name. He hides it from Noor, protecting them the way he always has. Emotional beat: protective love becoming its own kind of lie.

chapters.title: Counting Doors
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor counts eleven doors at night and twelve by morning, and behind the twelfth hears their mother's voice reciting the ritual's opening lines. Aunt Maren catches Noor listening and warns: some doors are kept shut by agreement, not locks. Emotional beat: the found family revealed as wardens — and jailers.

chapters.title: What the Frost Remembers
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel follows the frost patterns into the orchard and finds the missing ledger page: the ritual requires a twin's willing death, and their mother paid it with herself — or tried to. The frost wrote her final pattern unfinished. Emotional beat: devastating inheritance; duty revealed as a debt already half-paid.

chapters.title: The Elders' Supper
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The elders host a supper that is unmistakably a last meal, pressing Noor to sign the renewal before first frost. When Noor refuses, the mirrors stop lagging entirely — reflections now arrive before events, showing Noor's own death. Emotional beat: open war between love and obligation.

chapters.title: Which Twin Came Home
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Confronted by the pre-showing mirrors, Noor and Ansel finally test each other with childhood truths and discover the unbearable answer: the buried twin was Noor, and the one who came home has been Ansel all along, wearing the survival neither asked for. Emotional beat: identity shattered, then rebuilt — truth chosen over comfort.

chapters.title: The Final Pattern
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. First frost falls. Ansel goes alone to the orchard heart to finish his mother's pattern and die properly, but Noor arrives through the twelfth door, refusing to let him carry it solo. Emotional beat: climax of devotion — each trying to sacrifice for the other, neither willing to grieve again.

chapters.title: Two Offerings, One Bond
chapters.summary: Dual POV converging. Together they rewrite the ritual's final line — two names, willingly given, bound rather than spent — and the frost accepts, sealing itself around their joined hands instead of taking either life. They walk home past mirrors that reflect perfectly now, except one, forever empty. Emotional beat: resolution; love and duty reconciled at cost, found family remade on honest terms.
